I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads. On his horns were ten crowns, and on his heads, b', it moves through themes of lamb and dragon, victory and calls readers toward new creation.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows lamb and dragon lived out in patmos, persecution. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: Then I stood on the sand of the sea. I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads. On his horns were ten crowns, and on his heads, blasphemous names.
If anyone is to go into captivity, he will go into captivity. If anyone is to be killed with the sword, he must be killed. Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints.
Here is wisdom. He who has understanding, let him calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man. His number is six hundred sixty-six.

questions.question: What is happening in Revelation 13?
questions.answer: In 18 verses, this chapter revelation 13 (18 verses) continues the story of lamb and dragon. starting with 'then i stood on the sand of the sea. i saw a beast coming up out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads. on his horns were ten crowns, and on his heads, b', it moves through themes of lamb and dragon, victory and calls readers toward new creation. The setting is patmos, persecution, written to seven churches in asia. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote Revelation and why 13 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally john, addressed to seven churches in asia around ad 90-95. This chapter fits the book's purpose as apocalypse + letters — its themes of lamb and dragon, victory build on what came before.

questions.question: What does 'faith' mean in this chapter?
questions.answer: Trust, loyalty to God. In this chapter, it appears in context of lamb and dragon. For a first-time reader: think of it as trust, loyalty to god, not just religious jargon.

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through lamb and dragon and victory, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 14 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'He deceives my own people who dwell on the earth because of the signs he was granted to do in front of the beast, saying to those who dwell on the earth that they should make an im...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about lamb and dragon. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
